_comment: Real vulnerableVersionRange rows harvested from the GitHub Advisory Database via
`gh api graphql securityVulnerabilities` across 43 widely-used PIP and NPM packages.
Committed as a REGRESSION CORPUS so pinned-vuln-scan.py's range evaluator and version
comparator are tested against real advisory data offline, with no network in CI.
Two invariants are asserted over every row by `pinned-vuln-scan.py --self-test`:
1. every range parses -- an unparseable range must raise, never evaluate to 'safe';
2. no firstPatchedVersion falls inside its own vulnerableVersionRange.
That is 736 independent real-world facts exercising comparator and evaluator together.
The comparator was ALSO differentially tested against packaging.version over 144199
ordered pairs built from every version string here (100.0% agreement) and against the
semver spec section 11 precedence chain. packaging is only importable on 1 of the 4
interpreters on the dev machine, so it is a TEST-TIME ORACLE, never a runtime dependency.
Measured operator grammar over the 1122 advisory nodes these 736 unique rows came from,
which is why in_range EVALUATES operators rather than pattern-matching them:
The 15% using an INCLUSIVE upper bound or an exact pin would be silently missed by a
'>=,<'-only implementation. Version-string shapes include PEP440 pre-releases (2.6.0a1,
24.7.0rc1), npm pre-releases (15.6.0-canary.59, 3.0.0-beta.8), and 2- and 4-segment
releases -- 11.5% of version strings carry a pre-release tail.
No credential-shaped strings: CI scans full history with gitleaks, so a fixture that
trips it is a permanent build failure no later commit can undo.
Advisory data only ever GROWS, so a stale corpus stays valid: both invariants are
monotone, and re-harvesting can only add rows, never invalidate one.
